IMPLOSION: Omni-Global Files Chapter 11; CEO Ousted Amid Fraud & Civil Rights Probe

By Sarah Jenkins | Senior Financial Correspondent
Sept 17, 2018 | 08:45 AM EST

It took less than 48 hours for the "Titan of Century City" to be revealed as a paper tiger.

Omni-Global Media Corp. (OTC: OMGCQ), a company that marketed itself as a multi-national conglomerate, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection this morning in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Central District of California.

The filing location itself has raised eyebrows on Wall Street. Unlike most modern corporations, which incorporate in Delaware for legal protection, Omni-Global was revealed to be a standard California Corporation—subjecting it to the state's rigorous transparency laws and higher corporate tax rates.

Trading of OGM was halted at 9:30 AM. When it resumed on the Pink Sheets under the symbol OMGCQ, it opened at $0.12, down from Friday's close of $42.50.

The "Global" Mirage

The bankruptcy filing has exposed the company's "global footprint" as largely fictional. While their website lists satellite offices in London, Tokyo, and New York, the asset schedule reveals these are merely virtual mailboxes.

The company possesses zero international real estate. Their only physical asset is a lease for the 38th, 39th, and 40th floors of 2000 Avenue of the Stars in Los Angeles—a lease they have reportedly defaulted on.

"They spent more money on the naming rights for the building's exterior signage than they did on rent," said one forensic accountant reviewing the filing. "If you take a picture from the street, they look like they own the tower. In reality, they are tenants three months behind on payment."

The "Virginia" Catalyst

The collapse was triggered by a failed hostile takeover attempt of Engine Room Records, LLC, a boutique label based in Blacksburg, Virginia.

Omni-Global executives reportedly underestimated the target's sophistication. They were unaware that the label's CEO, Holly O'Connell, is not only a music executive but a credentialed attorney admitted to the Bar in Virginia, New York, Delaware, and California.

"They thought they were bullying a small-town manager," said legal expert Marcus Thorne. "They didn't realize she was licensed to practice law in their own backyard. She didn't need to hire local counsel to evict them; she is local counsel."

The Landlord Lockout

This morning, employees arriving at the headquarters were barred from entering by security. Pacific Rim Properties, LLC—the actual owner of the building—initiated a lockout at midnight.

In a twist of irony that has captivated the market, records show that Pacific Rim Properties is a wholly owned subsidiary of the O'Connell Family Trust. Omni-Global unknowingly tried to acquire their own landlord using bounced checks.

"It's a negotiation tactic. She's bluffing. Nobody evicts an anchor tenant over a few missed payments. We'll settle this in post-bankruptcy restructuring."
Senior Omni-Global Executive (Anonymous)

Sources close to the O'Connell family dispute this. "The eviction notice was served minutes after VP Jameson Frost insulted the lead singer, triggering a medical emergency. This isn't about rent. It's an execution."

Civil Rights Investigation

The Department of Justice has opened a preliminary inquiry into Omni-Global under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Leaked internal emails suggest executives targeted the company specifically because they viewed a disabled owner as "weak."
